[[EXPERIMENT_TITLE]] - Loading Isotherm Determination Report

Experiment Information

Experiment ID: [[EXPERIMENT_ID]]

Process ID: [[PROCESS_ID]]

Start Date: [[EXPERIMENT_DATE]]

End / Report Date: [[REPORT_DATE]]

Objective

Determination of loading isotherms for [[LIGAND_NAME]] binding to chromatography resin at different salt concentrations ([[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]) using an automated, robot-assisted workflow. Equilibration and loading conditions are standardized across [[NUMBER_OF_SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] salt conditions and [[NUMBER_OF_LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] ligand concentrations.

Methods

Overview of Automated Workflow

The experiment was executed on an integrated automated platform combining an Opentrons OT-2 liquid handler, a UR5 robot arm, a vacuum manifold with pump, and a Tecan Spark platereader. The workflow was designed to (i) equilibrate a filter plate packed with resin, (ii) load [[LIGAND_NAME]] solutions at different concentrations and salt conditions, (iii) separate bound and unbound ligand by vacuum filtration, and (iv) quantify remaining ligand in the filtrate by absorbance measurement.

Buffers, Ligand, and Resin
  • Buffer: [[BUFFER]]
  • Salt: [[SALT_NAME]] with stock concentration [[SALT_STOCK_CONCENTRATION]] [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]
  • Working salt concentrations: [[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]] (total of [[NUMBER_OF_SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] conditions)
  • Ligand: [[LIGAND_NAME]]
  • Ligand stock concentration: [[LIGAND_STOCK_CONCENTRATION]] [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]
  • Working ligand concentrations: [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]] (total of [[NUMBER_OF_LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] conditions)
  • Resin mass per well: [[RESIN_MASS]]
  • Total liquid volume per well: [[TOTAL_VOLUME]]
  • Number of replicate wells per condition: [[REPLICATES]]
Equilibration on Automated Platform

Resin-containing 96-deep-well plates and 96-well filter plates were handled by the UR5 robot, which positioned plates either on the Opentrons OT-2 deck or on the vacuum manifold connected to the pump.

  1. Initial setup:
    • The Opentrons OT-2 was configured using a custom labware definition (cytiva_96_filterwellplate_1ml.json) to correctly address the 96-well filter plate.
    • The UR5 transferred a deep-well plate ("96DeepWP") from storage to the pump position and placed the vacuum manifold.
    • The UR5 moved the filter plate between the OT-2 deck and the pump positions as required.
  2. Equilibration cycles:
    • For each of [[EQUILIBRATION_CYCLES]] equilibration cycles, the OT-2 dispensed equilibration buffer (total equilibration volume per cycle: [[EQUILIBRATION_VOLUME]]) onto the resin in the filter plate.
    • The UR5 transferred the filter plate to the vacuum manifold, where the pump applied vacuum at a speed of [[PUMP_SPEED]] for [[PUMP_DURATION]] seconds per cycle.
    • After each filtration step, the system waited for [[VENTING_TIME]] seconds to allow venting of the vacuum manifold.
    • The UR5 then returned the filter plate to the OT-2 deck, and the next cycle was executed.
    • The total equilibration time per cycle was approximately [[EQUILIBRATION_CYCLE_DURATION]] seconds.
Ligand Loading and Incubation
  1. Preparation of ligand solutions:
    • The OT-2 prepared or dispensed [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] [[LIGAND_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]] [[LIGAND_NAME]] solutions at the desired [[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]] conditions into the appropriate wells of the filter plate and/or deep-well plates, maintaining [[REPLICATES]] replicates per condition.
  2. Loading and incubation:
    • The OT-2 dispensed a total volume of [[TOTAL_VOLUME]] per well onto the equilibrated resin.
    • Plates were incubated at [[INCUBATION_TEMPERATURE]] with shaking at [[SHAKER_SPEED_INCUBATION]] rpm for [[INCUBATION_TIME]] to allow binding of [[LIGAND_NAME]] to the resin.
Filtration and Collection of Filtrate
  1. The UR5 transferred the deep-well collection plate to the pump position and re-installed the vacuum manifold.
  2. The UR5 moved the loaded filter plate from the OT-2 deck to the vacuum manifold above the collection plate.
  3. The vacuum pump was run at a speed of [[PUMP_SPEED]] for [[PUMP_DURATION]] seconds to pull the liquid through the resin and into the collection wells.
  4. The system then waited [[VENTING_TIME]] seconds for venting before the UR5 moved the filter plate to storage and returned the deep-well plate to the OT-2 deck for further handling if required.
Spectrophotometric Quantification
  1. The UR5 transferred the deep-well plate containing the filtrate to the OT-2 deck together with an empty measurement plate ("WP1").
  2. The OT-2 distributed aliquots of filtrate into the measurement plate, using fresh tips (300 µL) as prompted by the workflow.
  3. The UR5 transferred the loaded measurement plate to the Tecan Spark platereader.
  4. The Tecan Spark performed absorbance measurements at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm.
  5. Ligand concentrations were calculated from absorbance values using a linear calibration curve with slope [[CALIBRATION_CURVE_SLOPE]] and intercept [[CALIBRATION_CURVE_INTERCEPT]].

Results

Loading Isotherms of [[LIGAND_NAME]] on Resin
[[PLOT_1]]

Figure 1: Loading isotherms of [[LIGAND_NAME]] binding to resin at different salt concentrations ([[SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] [[SALT_CONCENTRATION_UNIT]]). Each curve represents the equilibrium binding of [[LIGAND_NAME]] to the resin as a function of feed ligand concentration, derived from filtrate concentrations measured at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm. Error bars (if shown) reflect replicate variability (n = [[REPLICATES]]).

Across the tested range of [[NUMBER_OF_SALT_CONCENTRATIONS]] salt conditions and [[NUMBER_OF_LIGAND_CONCENTRATIONS]] ligand concentrations, the automated workflow provided consistent loading profiles suitable for quantitative comparison of resin capacity and salt-dependent binding behavior.
